scenes.say: In Go, can a type implement an interface without saying so? Let's see how implicit interfaces work.

scenes.label: Methods
scenes.sub: A type matches an interface if it has all its methods.
scenes.say: A type matches an interface if it has all the methods the interface requires. No keywords needed.
Here, File has a Read method, so it automatically implements the Reader interface. No extra code.
Unlike Java or C sharp, Go doesn't need an 'implements' keyword. Just match the method set and you're done.

scenes.question: How do you declare interface impl in Go?
scenes.right: You don't declare it. If the methods match, it's automatic.
scenes.say: Don't fall for this: In Go, you never declare that a type implements an interface. It's all about matching methods.
